data: A cup of coffee coming down with me in the elevator on my lunch break from work. The placement of this mug on the cylindrical form of the balustrade communicates the precarity of walking a tightrope, much like talking office politics. Yet, the liquid finds a just level thanks to the mug’s leaning on the wall at just the right offset distance from the cylindrical surface.
A grand entrance to the driving range. The repeated interference patterns of the bellied netting create satisfying gradients, suspended in sunset.
The corrugation lines of this metal sheet reveal themselves as a ruled surface, twisted but solved.

A broken wine bottle with a derivative pun of a 1939 British propaganda poster: “keep calm and thrive”. A sculpture that embodies a hopelessly optimistic message despite its own damage followed by the completion of a large personal amount of alcohol – an allegory for my concluding journey in architecture school.
